prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all courses from academic years prior to the year in which this course is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and the ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of industrial engineering, specializing in Mechanics.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

Knowledge and skills to apply the fundamentals of concrete and metallic structure calculation to the design, repair, and reinforcement of structures. Design and calculation of overhead cranes. Understand the criteria, manage, and know how to apply regulations on the calculation and design of foundations and support bases.

Know the basic techniques of geotechnics and the principles of soil mechanics applied to the calculation of structural foundation elements. Have elementary notions of calculation on structural reinforcement, and structures of other materials.

syllabus_topics: Dimensioning and verification of structural elements in Service Limit States
Design and calculation of structural elements
Design and calculation of foundation elements
Notions of geotechnics and soil mechanics
Design and calculation of foundations. Typologies. Bases and supports on foundation elements
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum of 35% of the maximum score is required for both the objective questions exam and the development questions exam. Students who achieve a score equal to or greater than 45% in the sum of all exam components will receive 0.5 additional points for attending and participating in all laboratory practices and submitting required documentation, with another 0.5 points added for delivering all proposed homework problems. Students with an exam score equal to or greater than 40% will have their project work score added, up to a maximum of 1 point out of 10. Any unethical behavior, such as copying or plagiarism, will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for the entire academic year.
